newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Sheds $2/T amid ample supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Sheds $2/T amid ample supplies.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices shed $2.00 per tonne on Tuesday, weighed down by ample supplies, traders said.

Two cargoes of 180-cst for July 16-20 loading exchanged hands late Tueday at $96.50 and $97.00 per tonne with a local traders said to have purchased the supplies from a U.S and a European major respectively.
"Prices have slipped as they are enough supplies around," said one trader.
A major said a Kuwait cargo for July loading was also heard offered earlier in the day. But others said the cargo may have already been sold.
Traders were mixed on the near term outlook.
"The market could have hit a floor already and may move up as some demand sets in," said one Japanese trader.
But others said declining bunker demand and the lack of any strong buying indications from China would depress prices for a while.
Some traders said tender demand from Taiwan and Thailand should render support.
Thailand has issued a tender to buy 80,000 tonnes of fuel oil for August 15-25 delivery to Sri Racha.
The tender which seeks 75,000 tonnes of 180-cst grade, 2.0-percent sulphur and 5,000 tonnes of 180-cst, 1.0-percent fuel oil, closes today.
Taiwan has also issued a tender to buy two fuel oil grades for August 16-30 delivery, cost and freight Keelung, Taichung or Shenao basis. The tender will close July 8.
Traders also expected Chinese demand to pick up in August as buying interest so far has been scarce.
Swaps were also quoted lower, with July at $97.75/$98.25 and August at $97.75/$98.75, down from Monday's $98.25/$99.00 and $98.00/$98.75 respectively.
Asian LSWR prices are expected to firm with a reduced allocation of 2.3 million barrels from Indonesia in July, compared to about 3.1 million in June, traders said.
